scope: The named successor law amendment the axial-limb adjacency lane demanded: UPGRADE the touching-edge law metric from vertex-to-vertex (identify_bones_v2.py surface_gaps, which cannot see face-face contact through decimated triangle interiors) to the exact bidirectional point-to-triangle surface gap with a per-vertex k-escalation guarantee. The old metric stays reproducible for history; the new metric becomes the DEFAULT touching-edge measurement, as a CANDIDATE in tools/science_funnel/ with its own receipts. Pure geometry; no invention; the committed infant_skeleton.body.json is NOT modified.

rule_0.statement: The vertex-vertex law metric is a MEASUREMENT-RESOLUTION artifact, not a law of contact: for a vertex v, dist(v, nearest triangle of B) <= dist(v, nearest vertex of B) holds for every v because every vertex of B lies on a triangle of B, so the exact bidirectional point-to-triangle gap is a lower bound of the v2 number on every pair, while remaining an upper bound of the true surface-to-surface gap (its only admitted overestimate is the edge-edge-interior corner, where neither mesh owns the closest vertex -- named caveat, carried since the adjacency lane). The v2 metric therefore reads a FALSE REFUSAL exactly when a surface point of one bone lies inside the vertex-sparse interior region of a large decimated triangle of the other: contact exists, but no vertex pair sees it. The adjacency lane measured this artifact on the committed preview meshes: singleton 19's refined gap to the axial composite is 0.000 mm (a composite preview vertex lies ON a singleton-19 triangle) while the law metric reads 36.93 mm; singleton 14 shows the same pattern (refined 0.000 vs law 29.75 mm). A metric that reports a 36.93 mm refusal where the measured surfaces touch is measuring the mesh SAMPLING, not the anatomy. The upgraded law (exact point-to-triangle, per-vertex k-escalation certificate) measures contact directly: a measured 0.000 mm face-face gap IS contact and bonds; a measured 4.6 mm gap (shoulder) is still refusal and never self-grants.
rule_0.prediction: Registered BEFORE this lane ran any measurement. All numbers below that are already measurements come from the COMMITTED axial_adjacency_20260920 table (base 3539fdb9); predictions are about THIS lane's independent re-measurement of all 300 pairs and about the 264 pairs that lane never refined.  FLIP-SET (named): exactly TWO refused identifications become touching under the new default metric -- pair (1,19) (the task-named one: v2 36.93 -> point-to-triangle 0.000, composite vertex on a 19-triangle face) and pair (1,14) (the committed adjacency table already carries its 0.000 refined gap at law 29.75; honesty forbids pre-registering 19 alone when the committed record two directories over shows 14 in the same artifact class). Each flip becomes one candidate bond (bond.joint_01_14, bond.joint_01_19, material mat.cartilage per the committed bond law, rest_length = measured gap).  STAY-REFUSED (named): the two shoulders stay refused -- (1,4) point-to-triangle ~4.949 mm, (1,5) ~4.603 mm, both > 3.0 mm: a real cartilage-plus-soft-tissue joint gap at CT scale, not a sampling artifact. Singleton 16 stays isolated: its full 24-partner row stays > 3.0 mm under the new metric (prior row-min 5.815 mm to femur 2 at v2; the point-to-triangle number moves by vertex-sampling margins, not by 2.8 mm). Singleton 14's OTHER 23 partners stay refused (prior row-min 6.99 mm to foot 24); 14 joins the body ONLY through the composite contact.  NO-OTHER-FLIPS: among the 264 pairs the adjacency lane never refined, ZERO pairs cross from refusal (v2 > 3.0) to touching (new metric <= 3.0). Reasoning, not taste: the new-metric gap differs from the v2 gap only through triangle-interior approach, whose measured magnitude on this specimen is large exactly where the CT shows true contact ((1,14),(1,19) to 0.0) and small on genuine separations (shoulders moved 0.051/0.003 mm); a > 3.0 mm v2 refusal hiding a <= 3.0 mm face gap would be an intermediate artifact class with no member yet observed.  CUT STABILITY: under the new metric the touching class compresses (predicted class max ~2.911 mm at committed edge (2,6)) and the separation floor rises (predicted next non-touching ~4.603 mm at shoulder (1,5)); the v2-era cut 3.0 mm lands INSIDE the new valley, so the cut is RE-JUSTIFIED UNCHANGED, not re-chosen. The flip set is cut-independent: (1,14)/(1,19) enter the touching class at ANY cut > 0.0 mm.  COMPONENTS: with the committed 21 intra-chain bonds alone the body is 8 connected components (the committed honest reading); adding the 8 old-metric cross-component candidates closes it to 4; adding the 2 new-metric flips closes it to 2 (one body; singleton 16 the only isolate).  MONOTONICITY: point-to-triangle <= vertex-vertex on ALL 300 pairs (the derivation above), no exceptions.

rule_1_derivation_plan.note: No new free numbers. The new estimator, its guarantee, the cut, the resolution and the bond law are all inherited or derived; the only new numbers this lane produces are measurements.
rule_1_derivation_plan.metric_law_new_default: gap_new(A,B) = min( min_{v in V_A} dist(v, T_B), min_{v in V_B} dist(v, T_A) ) with T the preview mesh's triangle set, dist the exact Ericson point-to-triangle distance; certified per-vertex by k-escalation over triangle-centroid KD order: a vertex is exempt from deeper search iff dist_to_kth_centroid - R_max >= best_global (any unevaluated triangle for v lies >= kth_centroid - circumradius away), k quadruples for non-exempt vertices to a cap of n_tri (= full enumeration = unconditional guarantee). DERIVATION of the lower-bound property: every vertex of B is a point of T_B, hence min_{v} dist(v, T_B) <= min_{v} dist(v, V_B); the same holds mirrored, and monotone composition of mins gives gap_new <= gap_v2 identically. Both metrics are upper bounds of the true surface-surface gap; gap_new's only slack over truth is the edge-edge-interior corner (closest features on two edge interiors, neither mesh contributing a vertex) -- inherited, named, and unchanged from the adjacency lane's estimator, which this lane promotes verbatim.
rule_1_derivation_plan.metric_law_old_history: gap_v2(A,B) = min( min_{v in V_A} dist(v, V_B), min_{v in V_B} dist(v, V_A) ) on trimesh.load(preview, process=False) vertices, scipy cKDTree, float64 -- identify_bones_v2.py surface_gaps() verbatim, the metric that produced the 21 committed bonds. Kept as a first-class output column so the committed history stays reproducible forever.
rule_1_derivation_plan.cut_law: The cut is NOT re-chosen; it is RE-DERIVED by the same procedure that derived it for v2 (the shared empirical gap valley: last touching pair / next separated pair). Under the new default metric the same procedure runs on the new 300-pair distribution: valley_new = (max new-metric gap over the touching class, min new-metric gap over the non-touching class at the v2-era cut). The v2-era cut 3.0 mm is re-justified iff 3.0 lies in valley_new; if it does not, the derived cut is reported with the valley numbers and the classification stability/instability at the boundary is shown explicitly (which pairs change class at which cut). DERIVATION of why the valley can only widen: the new metric compresses true contacts toward 0 (measured: 9 of the 21 committed edges refine to 0.000) while true separations barely move (measured: shoulders 5.00 -> 4.949, 4.60 -> 4.603), so the class boundary sharpens; a cut valid for the blurrier metric inside the sharper valley remains valid.
rule_1_derivation_plan.resolution_law: 0.01 mm (committed gap_mm resolution) for both law columns; 0.001 mm for closest-point coordinates; float64 throughout; deterministic numpy reductions (first-index argmin ties).
rule_1_derivation_plan.bond_law: Unchanged from the committed matter_skeleton_import.py bond law: material mat.cartilage, cure 13 MPa (Yamada 1970), rest_length = measured gap. A 0.000 mm measured gap is contact: rest_length 0.0, cure applies. Candidate bonds are a DATA file for the law owner; this lane does not modify the committed body.
rule_1_derivation_plan.component_law: Union-find over the committed membrane graph (21 intra-chain bonds) plus the candidate cross-component set, reported at three stages: committed-only (must reproduce the committed 8), +old-metric candidates, +new-metric candidates.

discovery_degenerate_triangles.what: the preview meshes contain 314 EXACTLY-zero-area triangles (plus a sliver continuum down to |n|^2 ~ 2e-28 mm^4, measured). The point-to-triangle estimator promoted from the axial_adjacency_20260920 lane FORGES a 0.000 mm contact for any query vertex whose k-nearest-centroid shell contains one: the zero normal makes face_d = 0/1e-20 = 0 and a garbage face_ok. The first full run (unguarded, per the original promotion plan) produced 79 impossible 0.000 'flips' including pairs whose vertex-vertex gap is 101-107 mm -- geometrically impossible, which is what exposed the defect.
discovery_degenerate_triangles.guard_derivation: det = d11*d22 - d12^2 equals |ab x ac|^2 exactly (Lagrange identity); the barycentric face case is valid iff det > 64*eps_machine*d11*d22 (float64 roundoff of the product); below that the EXACT distance to the degenerate triangle is its edge minimum (error <= sliver height, ~1e-6 mm at the threshold for mm-scale edges -- below the 0.001 mm record resolution). The guard is relative (scale-free), not a tuned threshold.
discovery_degenerate_triangles.consequence_for_the_prior_lane: the committed axial_adjacency_20260920 refined_gap_mm numbers were produced by the SAME unguarded estimator: 14 of its 35 refined pairs are corrected here, all forged 0.000 -> real values ~= their v2 numbers (itemized in corroboration_vs_prior_lane). The named metric-artifact observation for singleton 19 was one of these forges.

verdicts.headline: THE REFUSALS STAND. The named successor work -- the bone-adjacency law metric upgrade -- lands as the candidate default (tools/science_funnel/surface_gap_metric.py): exact bidirectional point-to-triangle with the per-vertex k-escalation certificate AND the degenerate-triangle guard derived here. Under the corrected metric: ZERO refusal-to-touching flips (the mission-named singleton-19 composite bond does not exist -- its 0.000 evidence was an estimator forge; the true gap is 36.928 mm); the component count is unchanged (8 committed -> 4 with the standing 8 old-metric candidates -> 4 with the new metric); the 3.0 mm cut re-derives to the same valley it was derived from. The vertex-vertex law metric is CONFIRMED, not overturned: at this mesh density it under-measures face-face proximity by at most ~0.05 mm, never by enough to threaten a refusal.
